articles.title: After Starlink disruptions, Ukraine turns to Israeli tech to keep drones flying deep inside Russia
articles.summary: For Ukraine, losing a satellite connection could mean losing control of a drone flying deep inside enemy territory.
articles.body: For Ukraine, losing a satellite connection could mean losing control of a drone flying deep inside enemy territory.After repeated disruptions to Elon Musk's Starlink network exposed the risks of relying on a single provider, Kyiv is reportedly exploring an alternative developed by an Israeli company. The technology, manufactured in Italy, could give Ukrainian drones another way to stay connected during missions inside Russia.According to The Kyiv Post, Ukrainian forces are reportedly using satellite communication terminals developed by Israeli company HiSky on their long-range drones.The development comes amid growing concerns over restrictions affecting SpaceX's Starlink and military-focused Starshield services, which have become important to Ukraine's battlefield communications.The reported deployment came to light after Russian military sources circulated photographs of a Ukrainian drone that had reportedly crashed inside Russia.The recovered equipment appeared to include a satellite communication terminal identified as HiSky's SmartLITE system. Italian newspaper La Repubblica subsequently reported that the device carried a label identifying an Italian manufacturing facility in the province of Caserta.The claims received further support from a November 13 report by Germany's Handelsblatt, which said HiSky employees had confirmed that the company's six-kilogram terminals were being installed on Ukrainian drones.However, HiSky's chief executive declined to comment on the specific deployment, while Ukraine has not officially confirmed the reported operational use.What is HiSky and how does its technology work?HiSky is an Israeli satellite communications company founded in 2015. It develops compact satellite communication terminals for aircraft, ships, land-based vehicles and unmanned aerial vehicles (UAVs).Its SmartLITE family is designed to provide voice and data connectivity to mobile platforms. Unlike SpaceX, HiSky does not operate its own satellite constellation. Instead, its terminals connect to satellite networks operated by third-party providers.For Ukraine, the technology could offer an additional communication link for drones flying beyond the coverage of conventional ground-based systems. Satellite connectivity allows operators to receive flight information, monitor a drone's position and transmit mission-related instructions over long distances.One of the reported advantages of HiSky's system is its ability to connect through multiple commercial satellite networks. This could give Ukrainian forces greater flexibility if access to one network is restricted or disrupted.Ukraine's dependence on SpaceX's satellite communication network has become a growing concern for Kyiv, particularly after disruptions to its military-focused Starshield service.In October, Ukrainian officials reported that Starlink and Starshield terminals had stopped functioning on platforms travelling faster than approximately 160 kmph, affecting high-speed military drones. Although service was restored on October 24, the incident exposed the risks of relying on a network controlled by a private American company.The issue resurfaced in November when Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelenskyy complained that Starshield disruptions were affecting military operations, including efforts to intercept jet-powered Russian drones such as Iranian-designed Shaheds.He directed Ukrainian officials to engage with the US administration to resolve the problem. The repeated disruptions have strengthened Kyiv's case for diversifying its satellite communication infrastructure.HiSky's technology could provide an additional communication channel for long-range drones, reducing Ukraine's dependence on SpaceX, although it is not considered a complete replacement for Starlink.You use AI every day. articles.body: NEW DELHI: The Punjab Congress has formed a four-member committee to oversee the induction of leaders from other political parties, with the state heading into Assembly elections early next year.The panel, constituted by state Congress president Pargat Singh on Sunday, will coordinate the process and ensure consultations with local party leaders before any new entrant is admitted.The committee includes Congress Working Committee member and former MLA Vijay Inder Singla, MLA and deputy leader of the Congress Legislature Party Aruna Chaudhary, former MLA Kushaldeep Singh Dhillon and MLA Hardev Singh Laddi.According to the office order issued by the Punjab Pradesh Congress Committee, the panel will consult senior Congress leaders from the concerned area and the respective district Congress committee presidents before inducting any leader.The order states that the induction process will proceed only after their views have been taken into consideration and coordination with the local leadership has been ensured.The committee has been constituted with immediate effect.This move comes amid Congress's bid to strengthen its organisation and expand its political base ahead of the 2027 polls. articles.summary: NAVI MUMBAI: A 61-year-old chauffeur working for a builder in Nerul, who was allegedly assaulted and robbed of Rs 1,000 and his mobile phone by three men
articles.body: NAVI MUMBAI: A 61-year-old chauffeur working for a builder in Nerul, who was allegedly assaulted and robbed of Rs 1,000 and his mobile phone by three men while crossing Balaji Garden in Sector 20 on November 9, died during treatment at MGM Hospital in Kamothe on November 12.The Nerul police have added a murder charge to the robbery case registered against the three accused, who were arrested within 12 hours of the incident.The incident took place between 8.30am and 9am when the victim, Suresh Salve, was on his way to resume duty. He was a resident of Chembur and had worked as a chauffeur for the past 15 years for builder Gilbert D'Souza, who lives at Balaji Tower on Nerul Hill.Nerul senior inspector Ajay Kamble said the arrested accused include Shubham Nadkar (23), a Nerul Hill resident, and two minors aged 15, who live in Nerul village.Nadkar has been remanded to police custody, while the two minors have been sent to a juvenile remand home in Bhiwandi as per court orders.According to the FIR registered at Nerul police station on a complaint by Salve's daughter, Shilpa Sanjay Nanda (35), who lives in Ahmedabad, her father left home for work at 8am every day.After reaching Nerul railway station by train, he would walk to his employer's house at Balaji Tower. After finishing work, he would drop D'Souza home and walk back to the station to catch a train to Chembur.Nanda had come to stay with her parents in Chembur with her husband and children for Diwali. On November 9, her father left for work around 8am as usual, carrying his lunch box and a bottle of water in his backpack.Around 10am, D'Souza called Nanda's mother and informed her that Salve had been injured and taken to Terna Hospital in Nerul. Nanda rushed to the hospital and found her father in the ICU with severe injuries to his head, face and nose. He was unconscious.The family later learnt that Salve had been robbed of Rs 1,000 in cash, a mobile phone worth Rs 16,000 and his backpack containing a lunch box.Kamble said, "After registering the robbery case and recording statement of some eyewitnesses passing by the pathway, the three accused were arrested and the robbed cash and mobile was recovered from them. The accused claimed that they assaulted Salve after an argument over one of the accused accidentally pushing Salve while he was walking along the pathway."Stay updated with the latest Navi Mumbai news. articles.title: “What a match, Beta!”Virender Sehwag's parenting lesson after son Aaryavir's big win: Why children need humility more than trophies
articles.summary: A child's biggest achievement can become a parent's proudest moment. But what happens after the applause fades?
articles.body: A child's biggest achievement can become a parent's proudest moment. But what happens after the applause fades? How parents respond to a child's success can shape the way they handle their next failure, challenge or expectation. Former Indian cricketer Virender Sehwag shared this through a Instagram post celebrating his son Aaryavir Sehwag's performance in the U-19 Asia Cup 2026. His message carried a reminder about staying grounded, working hard and remembering what matters beyond trophies.Celebrate the achievement, but remind children that success is bigger than a trophyAaryavir had plenty to celebrate after India's dramatic one-wicket victory over Pakistan in the U-19 Asia Cup final. He scored 58 off 61 balls and finished the tournament with 361 runs in five innings, earning the Player of the Tournament award.But Sehwag's Instagram caption focused on something beyond the numbers. He wrote, "Some moments are bigger than awards, runs and trophies. These are the memories a father will cherish forever."He also wished that his son would always keep his feet firmly on the ground while reaching for greater heights through hard work and talent.It is a meaningful distinction for parents. Children should feel proud of what they achieve, but they should also understand that a medal does not determine their worth. A parent's appreciation should not disappear when the next result is less impressive.Watch the video here:ID@undefined Caption not available.ID@undefined Caption not available.Make room for nervousness instead of expecting children to be fearlessOne of the most touching moments from Sehwag's video call with Aaryavir was his admission: "Papa, I was so nervous… was just chanting Sita Ram, Sita Ram!"The young cricketer was recalling the tense final moments of the match. Despite his impressive performance, he was still a teenager experiencing the pressure of a major sporting occasion.This is an important reminder for parents who expect children to remain confident all the time. Even children who appear capable and composed can feel anxious when the stakes are high.Rather than dismissing nervousness as weakness, parents can make children feel comfortable talking about it. Sometimes, a child does not need a lecture or an immediate solution. They simply need to know that feeling scared does not make their achievement any smaller.Prepare children for comparisons instead of allowing them to define their identityBeing Virender Sehwag's son comes with its own expectations. Cricket fans will naturally compare Aaryavir's batting with that of his father, one of India's most celebrated opening batters.Sehwag has addressed this pressure in a recent interview with The Indian Express. He revealed that he has been preparing both his sons, Aaryavir and Vedant, for comparisons and criticism from childhood.His advice was straightforward: they should understand that comparisons will happen but focus on playing their own game.This is a valuable parenting lesson beyond sports. Children of successful parents can sometimes feel that they must match an established reputation. Parents can help by making it clear that a family legacy is not a performance target. Children deserve the freedom to build an identity that belongs to them.Let children understand the value of what they earnSehwag also spoke about teaching his sons financial responsibility. In a conversation on The Life Savers Show, he explained that his sons had started understanding the value of money after earning through cricket.He shared that spending from their own bank accounts made everyday expenses feel different. He gave the example of his sons spending Rs 7,000 on petrol and realising what that amount meant.Children may hear repeated advice about money, but responsibility becomes clearer when they experience the value of earning and spending it themselves.You use AI every day. articles.body: Akhilesh Yadav on Sunday sharpened the Samajwadi Party's Dalit outreach ahead of the 2027 Uttar Pradesh assembly elections. Calling for the BJP's ouster, he described Dalits as 'Damdar' (assertive).Addressing a Dalit Sammelan in Agra, the SP chief said the community would play a decisive role in defeating the ruling party.According to PTI, Akhilesh gave a new meaning to the 'D' in his party's PDA formulation, saying it now stood for 'Damdar Dalit'."Looking at the support of the Dalit community, I can say that the 'D' in our 'PDA' has now become 'Damdar Dalit'," he said. He described the gathering as the beginning of a broader movement for the upliftment of marginalised communities.PDA stands for 'Pichhda, Dalit and Alpsankhyak', referring to backward classes, Dalits and minorities. Akhilesh has positioned the formulation as the Samajwadi Party's social and electoral coalition against the BJP.Taking aim at the BJP, Akhilesh said, "This time, the Dalit community will defeat the BJP; wipe them out for good."He also warned that the ruling party would lose its political foothold in Agra, which he described as a stronghold the BJP had long considered secure.Attacking the government over alleged atrocities against Dalits, Akhilesh claimed that Uttar Pradesh had recorded the highest number of such cases, citing National Crime Records Bureau (NCRB) data.He further alleged that around 200 statues of Dr BR Ambedkar had been vandalised in the state over the past decade, without action against those responsible."Those who vandalise Dr Ambedkar's statues do not merely attack the sculpture. They attack the Constitution held in Babasaheb's hand," he said."If there is a Constitution, there is dignity. If there is a Constitution, there are rights. If there is a Constitution, there is democracy," Akhilesh added, accusing the BJP of following "Man Vidhan" instead of the Constitution.He also accused the BJP government of failing Dalit and backward-class students in higher education institutions and alleged that 26,000 primary schools attended by children from poor and Dalit families had been shut down.On employment and recruitment, Akhilesh alleged that question papers of more than 20 public examinations had been leaked in Uttar Pradesh, affecting young people's job prospects and reservation opportunities.Referring to the ongoing assistant teachers' recruitment protests over reservation, he promised that an SP government would ensure candidates received their due."This time, the lathi will lose and the laptop will win. The youth want to study and progress, but attempts are being made to intimidate them," he said, adding that the 2027 assembly elections would be a contest between five per cent and 95 per cent of the population.Akhilesh also criticised the BJP over its handling of government hospitals, alleged crimes against women and the condition of public education, promising that an SP government would ensure social justice, strengthen law and order and protect the rights of marginalised communities.Get the latest India News and Live updates. articles.title: US destroyer returns after 357 days at sea, longest deployment since WWII amid Iran war
articles.summary: More than 80 years after World War II, a US Navy destroyer has matched a wartime-era deployment milestone, spending nearly an entire year away from home.
articles.body: More than 80 years after World War II, a US Navy destroyer has matched a wartime-era deployment milestone, spending nearly an entire year away from home.The USS Spruance has returned after 357 days at sea, marking what is being reported as the longest deployment by an American destroyer since the Second World War. Its return, alongside another destroyer that spent 346 days deployed, offers a glimpse into the extraordinary demands the Iran war has placed on the US Navy.According to The War Zone (TWZ), the two Arleigh Burke-class guided-missile destroyers assigned to the USS Abraham Lincoln Carrier Strike Group returned to their homeports after spending 357 and 346 days at sea, respectively.The USS Spruance arrived at Naval Base San Diego on November 13, while the USS Michael Murphy returned to Joint Base Pearl Harbor-Hickam in Hawaii a day earlier.Both destroyers had initially set out for what was expected to be a routine deployment in the western Pacific. However, the escalation of the US-Iran conflict in February 2026 changed their mission.They were redirected to the Middle East, where they supported Operation Epic Fury, carried out missile strikes against Iranian targets and later enforced the US naval blockade of Iranian ports.Even after the USS Abraham Lincoln left the Middle East in August, the two destroyers remained in the region to support continuing blockade operations. Their extended assignments pushed their deployments well beyond the Navy's conventional seven-month cycle, with Spruance eventually spending 357 days away from home.US Navy's growing deployment crisisThe record-breaking deployments have exposed a growing problem for the US Navy. With military commitments stretching from the Middle East to the Indo-Pacific, the service is struggling to maintain its global presence without keeping warships at sea for longer periods.The Navy traditionally plans destroyer deployments for around six to seven months. However, the Iran conflict has pushed ships well beyond that cycle. Chief of naval operations Admiral Daryl Caudle has warned that deployments lasting 10 to 11 months could become more common.The US Navy operates just over 280 battle-force ships, including around 78 destroyers. These warships are expected to support operations across several regions, leaving limited room to rotate vessels without affecting other missions.Admiral Caudle has called for a bigger Navy, warning that the current fleet size is not sufficient to meet the country's growing operational demands.Keeping destroyers at sea for nearly a year also creates problems once they return. Warships require extensive repairs and maintenance after prolonged operations, reducing the number of vessels available for future missions.The extended deployments have added to an already growing maintenance backlog. USS Spruance, for instance, was originally scheduled for maintenance in July 2026, but its next maintenance period has been pushed to January 2027.

articles.title: A Virginia school built in 1884 to educate Black children during segregation became a storage building for about 60 years; after a $6.2 million restoration, its doors reopened November 14 as a museum
articles.summary: A historic school in Virginia that once provided education to Black children during the Jim Crow era has reopened as a museum and community centre.
articles.body: A historic school in Virginia that once provided education to Black children during the Jim Crow era has reopened as a museum and community centre. The former Union Street School in Leesburg has undergone a major refurbishment, giving the 1884 building a new purpose after decades of use as a storage facility. The museum officially opened on November 14, following a restoration project costing approximately £4.7 million ($6.2 million), according to the Loudoun County government project page.A new era as a community hubThe building, located in the heart of Leesburg, has been given a new role while keeping its historical importance. According to the Loudoun County project page, it will serve two main purposes: a museum and a community space. The museum will help visitors learn about Black education and community life in Loudoun County during racial segregation. The building will also provide space for community meetings and other local activities. The county's official project description says the work aimed to protect the building's historic structure while making it suitable for a working museum and educational centre. The project is also intended to tell a more inclusive story of the local community. Before the opening, the Loudoun County Sheriff's Office confirmed that Sheriff Chapman had been invited to attend the official ceremony and ribbon cutting. The event was scheduled for 10 a.m. on November 14.From landmark to storage facilityFor around 60 years, the building served a very different purpose. After the school stopped operating in 1958, it was used as a storage facility for Loudoun County Public Schools (LCPS). According to the county's historical account, LCPS later declared the property surplus and transferred it to the county government in 2019. The building's time as a storage facility meant it was no longer being used for the educational purpose for which it had originally been established. The restoration project was designed to bring the historic property back into public use while protecting its original features.Decades of learning under segregationThe Union Street School was established in 1884 as the Leesburg Training Center. It provided education to Black children from elementary school through high school during a period when racial segregation separated Black and white students. According to Loudoun County, the school played an important role in educating generations of African American students in Leesburg and nearby communities. Its closure in 1958 followed the opening of Douglass High School, the county's first high school for Black students, and a consolidated elementary school serving Black children in Leesburg. The building remains an important part of the area's African American history. It is recognised by the Virginia Department of Historic Resources and is included in the National Register of Historic Places. Its new museum role will give visitors an opportunity to learn about the students, teachers and wider community connected to the school. It will also help preserve memories of Black education during segregation.The path to preservation and memoryThe restoration required major work to make the historic building suitable for public use. According to Loudoun County's project information, the work included restoring historic windows, flooring and stonework. The project also added an entrance with an elevator, new toilets, structural improvements and updated fire protection systems. Accessibility upgrades were included to make the building easier for visitors to use. The county invested approximately $6.2 million in the project, according to its official announcement. The work was intended to protect the building's historic character while meeting modern safety and accessibility requirements. In 2023, the Loudoun County Board of Supervisors approved a lease agreement with the Loudoun Freedom Center through the county's Resident Curator Program. The organisation will manage the building and oversee its daily operations, maintenance and security. The county said the programme aims to protect historic properties that are no longer fully used while making them available to the public. The November 14 event marked the completion of the restoration. According to the county's announcement, the programme included an 11 a.m. ribbon-cutting ceremony, followed by an open house from noon until 2 p.m. Former students were expected to share their memories and experiences with visitors. The Loudoun Freedom Center Museum at Union Street will now provide a permanent space to explore African American history and education in Loudoun County.You use AI every day. articles.title: Watch: Forest staff chase lion on motorcycles at Gujarat safari park, 3 relieved of duty
articles.summary: RAJKOT: Three outsourced forest personnel were relieved of their duties after a video purportedly showing them chasing a lion on a motorcycle at Ambardi
articles.body: RAJKOT: Three outsourced forest personnel were relieved of their duties after a video purportedly showing them chasing a lion on a motorcycle at Ambardi Safari Park in Gujarat's Amreli district went viral on social media, an official said on Sunday."We had launched an inquiry into the incident. Some forest personnel were directing the lion towards its 'kraal' in the safari park in the evening. Usually, this routine exercise is carried out using a jeep, but some personnel used motorcycles," principal chief conservator of forests Jaipal Singh told PTI.Singh said a notice was issued following the incident and the three outsourced forest staff were relieved of their duties.In-charge assistant conservator of forests (ACF) Mitesh Vaniya said the video was recorded during the Diwali festival. However, he denied that the lion had been harassed."The safari park spans over 300 hectares, and every day at 5pm, the lions are fed in a 100x100-metre fenced area called a kraal. The officials in the video spotted a lion straying from the kraal and were directing it towards the enclosure. articles.summary: NEW DELHI: Security forces on Sunday launched a cordon and search operation in Jammu and Kashmir's Kulgam district after receiving inputs about the
articles.body: NEW DELHI: Security forces on Sunday launched a cordon and search operation in Jammu and Kashmir's Kulgam district after receiving inputs about the presence of terrorists suspected to be behind an attack on a CRPF post earlier this week.The operation is under way in Khudwani and adjoining areas of the south Kashmir district following an input from the J&K Police about the presence of terrorists, officials said according to news agency PTI.Senior Army officers, Director General of Police Nalin Prabhat and Kashmir Range Inspector General of Police Sujit Kumar Singh are overseeing the operation.Security forces have sealed all entry and exit points in the area, the officials added. The search operation follows an attack on a CRPF checkpoint in Kulgam on Wednesday afternoon.Around 2.15 pm, two motorcycle-borne assailants opened fire on CRPF personnel before fleeing the spot, injuring three personnel.The injured were taken to a hospital in Anantnag district for treatment.Security forces have been searching for the attackers for the past four days, with senior officers supervising the operation.In a separate incident in Kishtwar, the bullet-riddled bodies of two Special Police Officers (SPOs), who went missing on Wednesday, were recovered on Thursday morning.Get the latest India News and Live updates. articles.title: 'No place for goons': CM Adhikari's warning to criminals after encounter of Shantiniketan accused
articles.summary: West Bengal Chief Minister Suvendu Adhikari on Sunday warned criminals and people possessing illegal firearms to leave the state.
articles.body: West Bengal Chief Minister Suvendu Adhikari on Sunday warned criminals and people possessing illegal firearms to leave the state. His warning came after Ratan Sheikh, the prime accused in the Santiniketan shooting case, was killed in a police encounter in Birbhum's Nanoor.Speaking to news agency ANI, Adhikari said Sheikh had opened fire at police personnel when they attempted to arrest him. He said the police took necessary action in response."He shot at the police, and the police did what needed to be done on the spot. It would not be appropriate for me to comment on this. There is no place for goons and rapists in West Bengal," Adhikari said.Issuing a warning to criminals and those possessing illegal firearms, he added, "Even now, whatever remaining goons and those with illegal arms are left, flee from here; leave immediately. There is no place for them here."Sheikh was accused of opening fire at a police team that went to arrest him in connection with the Santiniketan shooting incident. The firing took place on Friday evening in the Layek Bazar area of Bolpur.Three police personnel had reached the area to apprehend Sheikh. However, he allegedly opened fire after spotting them, injuring constable Biswajit Das in his left leg. Sheikh fled the spot and had been absconding since the incident.Sheikh was killed in a police encounter in Nanoor on Sunday. Adhikari described him as a dreaded criminal and said 36 cases had been registered against him. Sheikh had been granted bail in a robbery case and returned to the area last Friday.Following the shooting, Adhikari visited injured constable Biswajit Das at Bardhaman Medical College and Hospital. articles.body: Nashik: The crime branch’s Unit-3 has arrested a history-sheeter wanted in the murder of Nashik Road resident Sumit Pagare, taking the total number of accused held in the case to 17.Rahul Sonawane (35), a resident of Chavan Mala on Jai Bhawani Road in Upnagar, was arrested on Saturday from a flat on Dindori Road in Mhasrool after police received a tip-off about his whereabouts. He had been on the run for nearly three months since the murder.Sonawane is accused in the Aug 17 murder of Pagare, who was allegedly shot in the Nashik Road area over a turf war and supremacy dispute. Police said Pagare had earlier been arrested in a mephedrone trafficking case along with his elder brother and others, and was killed a few months after securing bail in the matter.Acting on specific information received by constables Charudatta Nikam and Bhushan Sonawane, a crime branch team tracked down and arrested the suspect from his hideout in Mhasrool.Police said Sonawane was also wanted in a grievous hurt case registered with Upnagar police station last year.“Rahul Sonawane is a history-sheeter with multiple serious offences registered against him, including murder, attempt to murder, attempt to dacoity, robbery, theft, extortion, illegal firearms-related offences and narcotics trafficking,” a police officer said.According to investigators, more than 20 criminal cases are registered against him across police stations in Nashik city, Nashik rural and Jalgaon districts.The arrest operation was carried out under the guidance of police commissioner Sandeep Karnik by a team led by senior inspector Jagvendrasingh Rajput of crime branch Unit-3.Police said all 17 accused arrested in the Pagare murder case have been booked under the Maharashtra Control of Organised Crime Act (MCOCA).You Can Also Check: Gold Rate in Nashik | Silver Rate in Nashik | Bank Holidays in Nashik | Public Holidays in Nashik | Petrol Price in Nashik | Diesel Price in Nashik | CNG Price in Nashik | LPG Price in NashikStay updated with the latest Nashik news. articles.title: Fines fail to curb cattle on roads; lax enforcement draws flak
articles.summary: Madurai residents slam lax enforcement as stray cattle keep roaming roads despite Rs 4.14 lakh fines; corporation plans more impounding and auctions.
articles.body: Madurai: Residents and daily commuters in Madurai continue to face severe safety hazards and traffic bottlenecks as stray cattle roam unchecked through residential streets and public areas. While Madurai corporation has been conducting periodic impounding drives, residents say the scale of enforcement is too sluggish to curb the growing menace.Corporation data from June shows that 94 stray cattle heads have been impounded in municipal pounds, with owners facing fines totaling Rs 4,14,500. However, residents point out that impounding fewer than 100 animals over several months does little to clear major thoroughfares of the herds which routinely block traffic and endanger two-wheeler riders.D Raghavan, president of Gomathipuram Resident’s Welfare Association, said the corporation’s cattle impounding vehicles operate only in the mornings. “Most of the troubles we face with cattle are at night, when they lie down and block the road and visibility is poor. Cattle are left to roam in the evenings and despite fines being paid, the problem persists,” he said.“Navigating Vaigai riverbank roads and interior lanes after dark has become a nightmare because bovines suddenly step out into oncoming traffic, leading to frequent near-misses,” said K Karthikeyan, a resident of Anna Nagar. “Fining owners a few thousand rupees clearly isn’t working because the same animals are back on the streets within days after the fines are paid,” he added.Shopkeepers and pedestrians echo similar frustrations, noting that uncollected garbage and open waste frequently attract cattle into commercial hubs, creating unhygienic conditions. “Sometimes the cattle get aggressive near market stalls and block the entire footpath, forcing elderly people and schoolchildren to walk onto busy roads to avoid them,” said M Selvi, a resident near Simmakkal.While Madurai corporation reiterates its warning that cattle owners must confine their animals to private sheds or face public auctions or transfers to gashalas for repeat offences, residents say sporadic crackdowns are insufficient to resolve the problem.A senior corporation official said cattle catching and impounding activities will be increased in the coming days. “Apart from fines, repeat offenders will have their cattle seized and auctioned off rather than be returned,” the official said.You Can Also Check: Gold Rate in Madurai | Silver Rate in Madurai | Bank Holidays in Madurai | Public Holidays in Madurai | Madurai AQI | Weather in Madurai | Petrol Price in Madurai | Diesel Price in Madurai | CNG Price in Madurai | LPG Price in MaduraiStay updated with the latest Madurai news. articles.title: 'Divide-and-rule tactics': RSS chief Bhagwat's warning over attempts to split India
articles.summary: NEW DELHI: RSS chief Mohan Bhagwat on Sunday warned of attempts to divide India by exploiting smaller identities.
articles.body: NEW DELHI: RSS chief Mohan Bhagwat on Sunday warned of attempts to divide India by exploiting smaller identities. He compared the efforts to the British-era policy of divide and rule and called for national unity.Addressing the 'Maru Ninad-2026' Ghosh Shivir organised by the RSS Jodhpur Prant at Rajaram Ashram in Shikarpura, Bhagwat said India was moving in the right direction. However, certain global forces did not want the country to become a great nation, ANI reported."India is the treasure trove of everyone's hopes. But the state of the world is very strange. For their own selfish reasons, they don't even want India to become great," Bhagwat said.He alleged that attempts were being made to create divisions by magnifying smaller identities and provoking conflicts among people. He compared these tactics to those used during British rule.The RSS chief urged people to shed selfishness, petty differences and ego. He stressed the need to build an organised society rooted in Dharma and national service.Citing the Mahabharata, Bhagwat explained how internal discord could weaken even a powerful force. He pointed out that the Kauravas had an army of 11 Akshauhinis and powerful warriors such as Bhishma, Dronacharya, Karna and Ashwatthama. Yet, they lost because of internal differences.In contrast, the Pandavas won with an army of seven Akshauhinis because they remained united and resolved their differences to preserve harmony, he said.Bhagwat also highlighted the importance of grassroots leadership. He said every village, street and neighbourhood needed 25 to 100 selfless individuals of good character who stood with people during their moments of happiness and sorrow and remained dedicated to the country.Speaking about the RSS Ghosh programme, Bhagwat traced the tradition of battlefield music to ancient Indian texts, including the Bhagavad Gita. He referred to the sacred conches Panchajanya and Devadatta, whose blowing marked the beginning of the Mahabharata war.He said early RSS volunteers initially learned musical compositions from British military bands. However, a sense of self-respect inspired them to develop original martial compositions based on Indian classical music theory.Bhagwat said RSS band performers did not play music for personal recognition or applause. Instead, the programme aimed to inculcate discipline, selflessness and teamwork and promote collective progress, he added.Get the latest India News and Live updates. Download the TOI app.

articles.title: Prince William, Kate to meet PM Modi in Delhi during three-day India visit
articles.summary: Prince William and Kate Middleton will meet Prime Minister Narendra Modi in New Delhi during their upcoming India visit, as the royal couple look to
articles.body: Prince William and Kate Middleton will meet Prime Minister Narendra Modi in New Delhi during their upcoming India visit, as the royal couple look to strengthen ties between the United Kingdom and one of its key international partners, The Independent reported.The meeting on Wednesday will be a major part of the couple's three-day visit, which begins on Monday, November 16.The engagement reflects William's growing role in supporting Britain's diplomatic relationships through overseas visits and the monarchy's soft power.Modi is expected to return to New Delhi from the Philippines, where he is attending an official engagement, to meet the royal couple. William and Kate last visited India in 2016, when they also met the Indian prime minister.A Kensington Palace spokesperson said the UK and India shared an important relationship, with growing links across trade, investment, defence, security, technology, education and culture.The meeting, the spokesperson added, would provide an opportunity to celebrate and strengthen ties between the two countries.Discussions are expected to cover areas including climate change and the Commonwealth, while the visit will also highlight cultural and sporting connections between India and Britain.The couple will spend much of their visit in Mumbai, which is hosting the 2026 Earthshot Prize awards. They are expected to engage with Bollywood personalities and celebrate India's passion for cricket. Their programme will begin with a game of street cricket, highlighting the sporting links between the two countries.The highlight of the visit will be the Earthshot Prize ceremony on Tuesday, November 17. Winners in five categories will each receive £1 million for their work on solutions to environmental challenges. The prize, founded by William, is now in its sixth year.Kate is also expected to take part in engagements linked to her early-years work. Her presence alongside William marks a significant moment, as this is her first long-haul overseas trip since she announced her cancer diagnosis in March 2024.A Kensington Palace spokesperson said Kate was “enormously proud” of William's work on Earthshot and was looking forward to joining him for one of the most important moments in his year.The visit will also feature the first children's Earthshot initiative, which has involved one million schoolchildren across 15,000 schools in 24 Indian states.You use AI every day. articles.body: US treasury secretary Scott Bessent on Sunday said Nvidia should look outside the firm for a new chief executive, citing concerns over the company's internal culture."This makes me think that as the board conducts a search for a new leader that they need to go outside the company, that just (with) what was going on inside the company, they need a dramatic shakeup," Bessent told Fox News' Sunday Morning Futures.Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang stepped down on Thursday after reports emerged about his alleged extramarital relationships, including one involving Alice Huang, a former senior executive at Megaspeed International, an Nvidia customer, who was reportedly under US investigation on suspicion of spying for China.Bessent also said Nvidia's board and its external legal advisers should answer questions about the company's compliance culture and adherence to US export restrictions within the next 10 days.Earlier this week on November 10, Nvidia's independent board members announced that they had appointed the Wall Street law firm Wachtell, Lipton, Rosen & Katz to conduct an independent investigation.The decision followed reports by The New York Times and The Wall Street Journal about Huang's relationships with Alice Huang and US authorities' suspicions that she may have been spying for China.Beijing has denied that Alice Huang is a spy. In an interview with Bloomberg published on October 29, Jensen Huang said the US government had not informed him about its suspicions concerning her.In a statement earlier this week, Huang apologised for being unfaithful to his wife and disappointing the company, although he did not specifically name Alice Huang.You use AI every day.
